messages:
customer_jd: hi team, hitting partial SSE output from your hosted endpoint when we go through our internal grpc-gateway. client sees a few events then the stream is cut with an RST_STREAM. no error body. logs show HTTP/2 RST_STREAM(2) on upstream. repro attached below.

alex_support: sorry you're blocked — can you paste the minimal repro + headers? is the gateway terminating TLS or proxying h2? also send the request id if available. :wave:

customer_jd: repro steps: 1) call our gateway which translates grpc->grpc-web (text), 2) it forwards to redwood hosted /v1/stream with Accept: text/event-stream, 3) we get 2-3 events then client disconnects. curl command we used:

```

curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://my-gateway.company.internal/proxy/redwood/v1/stream?prompt=hi

```

customer_jd: gateway is envoy 1.26 as an ingress, configured to convert grpc->http1 for browser clients (grpc-web). tls is terminated at envoy, upstream uses h2 to redwood.

deploy-bot: automatic alert: 2024-11-04T13:12:03Z upstream reset observed (trace: trc-9f2b).

maria_runtime: thanks for the detail. two likely classes: 1) envoy/grpc-web transform is coalescing or adding content-length which breaks chunked SSE expectations, or 2) h2 flow-control/kvs gets RST if stream window shrinks due to intermittent client ack. do you see any 'Content-Length' or 'grpc-status' headers in the final frames?

customer_jd: no content-length on the request. headers forwarded:

```
:method: GET
:scheme: https
:authority: my-gateway...
accept: text/event-stream
authorization: Bearer **REDACTED**
user-agent: curl/8.2
```

alex_support: can you capture the raw h2 frames between envoy and redwood? if not, tcpdump of the flow plus the redwood request id (from deploy-bot trace) will help. also does your gateway buffer to completion before proxying? some gateways buffer a small amount and then flush in one chunk leading to partial events.

customer_jd: attaching a small pcap snippet (we trimmed) — shows RST_STREAM from upstream after ~2.6s. i also saw fragmented last event (no terminating \n\n).

sre_jen: quick check: are you using http1.1 keepalive on the front and multiplexing to h2 upstream? we've seen cases where intermediaries (esp grpc-web adapters) rewrite transfer-encoding or inject chunk coalescing. if envoy squeezes frames and then sees a downstream close it might send an RST upstream.

maria_runtime: workaround to validate: force the gateway to use proxy_buffer_size small and disable http1->http2 content-length insertion, or set envoy to flush on chunk (streaming flush) so SSE chunks are forwarded immediately. example envoy config snippet to preserve streaming: 

```
# envoy route config (example)
route:
  cluster: redwood_upstream
  per_filter_config:
    envoy.filters.http.buffer:
      disable_chunked_encoding: false
      max_request_bytes: 0
    envoy.filters.http.stream_idle_timeout: 0s
```

maria_runtime: also try switching the upstream to plain HTTP/1.1 (if possible) as a test — if the issue goes away it's likely an h2 flow-control framing edge with your gateway translation.

customer_jd: tried forcing h1 upstream via envoy, that actually made the stream stable. so looks h2-related. any suggestions to avoid RSTs?

alex_support: for a targeted fix we can: 1) add a fallback policy on our side to accept long-lived http1 streaming proxied through gateways, or 2) add a header you can set (x-redwood-stream-mode: buffering|passthrough) that will adjust how we advertise window sizes / keepalive pings. i'll escalate to runtime for option 2. in the meantime keep using the h1 passthrough.

maria_runtime: filing an internal ticket to investigate h2 RST behavior from our side when peer windows are small + intermediary grpc-web adaptors. if you can share the trace id (trc-9f2b) PM me and i'll link logs.

customer_jd: sending trace id in DM. thanks all, using h1 workaround for now. :pray:
